sessionClaim.description: JWT claim used to identify the session

sessionSourceName.description: Session Source Name (header / cookie / body field)

fields.name: path
fields.description: The path to listen on (e.g. "my-hook")

fields.name: method
fields.description: HTTP Method to listen for

fields.name: responseMode
fields.description: When to respond to the webhook request

fields.name: authentication
fields.description: The type of authentication to use for incoming webhook requests

fields.name: sessionSource
fields.description: How the platform identifies the caller for per-user session continuity. Required when memory or loops should partition by caller.

fields.name: sessionSourceName
fields.description: Header name, body field path, or cookie name used as the caller id.

fields.name: basicAuthUser
fields.description: The username for Basic Authentication

fields.name: basicAuthPassword
fields.description: The password for Basic Authentication

fields.name: headerAuthName
fields.description: The header name to check for authentication

fields.name: headerAuthValue
fields.description: The expected header value for authentication

fields.name: jwtSecret
fields.description: The secret key used to verify the JWT token

fields.name: jwtAlgorithm
fields.description: The algorithm used to sign the JWT token

fields.name: sessionClaim
fields.description: The claim in the JWT payload that identifies the user (e.g. sub, email, userId). Leave blank to skip session tracking.

fields.name: requireRoleCheck
fields.description: If enabled, the incoming JWT must contain an authorized role claim to execute the workflow.

fields.name: roleClaimKey
fields.description: The field name inside the JWT payload that contains the user's role (e.g., "role", "groups").

fields.name: allowedRoles
fields.description: A comma-separated list of roles that are allowed to trigger this workflow. If empty, all roles pass.

fields.name: allowedOrigins
fields.description: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS. Use * to allow all origins.

fields.name: binaryDataFieldName
fields.description: The name of the field in the request that contains binary data (for file uploads).

fields.name: ignoreBots
fields.description: If enabled, requests from known bots (crawlers, spiders) will be ignored.

fields.name: ipAllowlist
fields.description: Comma-separated list of IPs or CIDR ranges. Only these IPs can trigger the webhook.

fields.name: noResponseBody
fields.description: If enabled, the webhook will respond with an empty body (only status code).

fields.name: rawBody
fields.description: If enabled, the raw request body will be passed as-is without parsing.

fields.name: responseData
fields.description: Custom response data to return when the webhook is triggered (JSON or text).

body.guidelines_text:
BRIGHTFOLD STUDIO — BRAND GUIDELINES

COLOUR
The primary green is #2F5D50. It anchors headers, calls to action, and navigation. It should never dominate more than a quarter of any composition.
Secondary sand #D9C7A3 carries background fills and large surfaces. It should feel like paper, not like a highlight.
Accent rust #C4622D is reserved for a single emphasis per layout. Two accents in one design is one too many.
Never introduce colours outside this palette. Tints and shades of the three approved colours are permitted.

LOGO
The wordmark appears top-left in all horizontal formats and centred in square formats.
Minimum clear space around the logo is equal to the height of the letter B in the wordmark.
Never stretch, rotate, recolour, or add effects to the logo. Never place it on a busy photograph.
Use the light logo on dark surfaces and the dark logo on light surfaces. There is no third variant.

PHOTOGRAPHY
Imagery is candid and unstyled, shot in daylight, never on seamless backdrops.
Photograph products in context — on a desk, in a hand, beside the objects people actually use them with.
Never photograph on pure white cyclorama. Never use studio strobes that flatten shadows.
Avoid stock-photo gestures: pointing at laptops, laughing at salads, handshakes over conference tables.
People may appear in photographs, but they are never the subject. The work is the subject.

EFFECTS AND TREATMENTS
Avoid heavy drop shadows, gradient overlays, glows, and bevels.
A single soft shadow at low opacity is permitted to lift a card off its background. Nothing stronger.
Do not blur backgrounds artificially. If depth is needed, capture it in the photograph.

TYPOGRAPHY
Headings are set in Bitter. Body copy is set in Source Sans 3. No third typeface.
Headlines run three to six words. Longer headlines mean the idea is not yet clear.
Body copy explains rather than persuades. Two sentences per paragraph is the ceiling.
Never set body copy below 14 pixels or in all capitals.

VOICE AND TONE
The voice is direct and unhurried. State the benefit and stop.
Do not use exclamation marks. Do not use urgency language such as "hurry", "limited time", or "act now".
Write in the second person. Address one reader, not an audience.
Contractions are welcome. Jargon is not.

CLAIMS AND SUBSTANTIATION
Any claim about materials or sourcing must name the specific supplier or certification.
Never use the word premium without stating what makes it so.
Sustainability claims require a measurable figure and a source. "Eco-friendly" alone is not acceptable.
Comparative claims must reference the specific competitor product and the date of comparison.

LAYOUT AND SPACING
The base spacing unit is 8 pixels. All margins and padding are multiples of it.
Generous white space is a feature, not wasted room. When in doubt, remove an element rather than shrink it.
Left-align text in all formats. Centred body copy is not used.

ACCESSIBILITY
Text on the primary green must use the sand or white for a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1.
Never convey meaning through colour alone. Pair every colour signal with a label or icon.
All images require alternative text describing what the image shows, not what it is called.
